synopsis: Magic Formula, also called Pacejka, is an empirical tire model fitted to test data and widely used for road vehicles [f13780]. Chapter 8 identifies it alongside Fiala for rigid full-vehicle multibody models with 3–8 degrees of freedom that predict braking-related roll, yaw, jackknife and pitch stability, plus load transfer [f6447]. Its terrain scope is limited: the glossary says Magic Formula, Fiala and TMeasy assume a firm surface, while Project Chrono developers report that these handling tire models do not work with deformable terrain [f13782, f8498]. For deformable-terrain simulation in Chrono, the reported compatible options are rigid or FEA tires and tracked vehicles, so the braking-model capability should not be read as establishing suitability for deformable off-road ground [f8498, f6447].

relations.note: Defines Magic Formula's empirical basis and road-vehicle use, complementing its braking-dynamics application.
Adds the firm-surface assumption to the tire models used for braking-stability prediction.
Chrono developers' reported incompatibility with deformable terrain supports the glossary's firm-surface limitation.
Limits applicability in Chrono: handling tires cannot extend these predictions to deformable terrain.
Identifies Pacejka as Magic Formula, connecting Chrono's reported limitation to the named model.
